title: Storage & Drive Health
description: Capacity first, then the drives underneath it: NVMe, SATA SMART, and ZFS.

options.content:
Capacity first, because a full filesystem takes a service down faster than a dying disk does.

---

panels.title: ZFS pools online
panels.description: Seven datasets on hddpool-1, on grey-server. Only grey-server has a ZFS pool; the two LXC guests that appear to have one are reading its kernel.

panels.title: NVMe critical warnings
panels.description: Any non-zero value is the drive itself asking for attention.

panels.title: SMART self-assessments failing
panels.description: Only disks that actually report a self-assessment are counted. Both QEMU guests expose a virtual disk with none, which is absent rather than failed.

targets.expr: count(smartmon_device_smart_healthy == 0 and on (host, disk) smartmon_device_smart_available == 1) or vector(0)

options.content:
Every real mount in the fleet. Pseudo-filesystems are excluded — they say nothing about capacity.

---

panels.title: Filesystem headroom
panels.description: `Free in 30d` extrapolates the last six hours forward a month. It is a straight line through noisy data, so read it as a direction, not a date — but a negative number there is a mount worth watching.

panels.title: Filesystem fill — eight tightest
panels.description: Top eight. The table above covers every mount.

options.content:
Physical devices only. On an LXC guest these are the node's disks, not the guest's, because /proc/diskstats is not namespaced.

---

panels.title: Utilisation — eight busiest devices
panels.description: Share of wall time the device had at least one request in flight. Sustained 100% is a saturated disk.

options.content:
The four NVMe drives that report SMART data, on purple, blue, red and green.

---

panels.title: NVMe health
panels.description: `Written` converts the NVMe data-unit counter, which counts 1000 × 512-byte units.

panels.title: Endurance used
panels.description: The drive's own wear estimate. 100% means it has written its rated endurance, not that it has failed.

options.content:
The four spinning and SATA-SSD drives that report a SMART self-assessment.

---

panels.title: SMART
panels.description: Reallocated, pending and CRC counts are the three that matter: any of them climbing is a drive on the way out, whatever the overall assessment still says.

options.content:
hddpool-1 on grey-server, the fleet's only ZFS pool.

---

panels.title: ARC size
panels.description: The adaptive replacement cache, in RAM. It grows to fill what it is allowed.

panels.title: ARC hit ratio
panels.description: Clamped so an idle pool reads 0 rather than dividing by zero.
